newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar succumbs to heavy selling.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar succumbs to heavy selling.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed at the bottom of its range on Wednesday after succumbing to heavy selling in the morning.
Dealers said a U.S. investment house dumped the Kiwi heavily triggering stop losses around 0.6850 which drove it lower still.
It ended at 5.15 p.m. (0515 GMT) at US$0.6838/43 after trading a 0.6830-68 range.
The Trade-Weighted Index closed at 67.93 from 68.16 at the opening.
Dealers said comments from Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash that the bank had not changed the settings of its desired conditions target did nothing to change sentiment.
A Wellington bank chief dealer said most people had drawn their own conclusions about the state of the economy and the RB's view tended to lag others'.
He expects any rallies about 0.6850 to be sold into and that would also keep the TWI pegged back.
